title: Restrict evidence exemptions to historical bootstrap features
acceptance_criteria: Existing historical bootstrap entries retain their evidence exemption explicitly.
New normal completed work requires a non-empty local or remote work-item reference and normal evidence.
Omitting the issue field cannot silently grant a new feature the legacy exemption.
Focused contracts cover historical compatibility, newly untracked work, and valid local identifiers.

title: Document and verify a minimal bootstrap adoption path
acceptance_criteria: One concise adoption map labels core files to copy, project files to adapt, source history to omit, and optional capabilities.
First-run instructions specify runtime, package installation, and Git-base prerequisites.
A minimal adoption fixture demonstrates the documented project extension without copying sample product state.
Metrics and impact analysis remain optional and no generator or new orchestration framework is introduced.
Primary adoption entry points link the map and focused adoption contracts pass.

title: Reduce routine harness coordination and verification cost
acceptance_criteria: Routine work defaults to one implementer who also plans and finalizes and one independent reviewer; a separate coordinator is optional. Instructions limit context, handoffs, and repeated checks.

Review refreshes inspect the changed scope and retain one canonical approval, using Git history for committed prior approvals and preserving uncommitted prior evidence. Whole-index binding and required gates remain intact; dependent PR stacks are not the default.
Remove tests that police prose wording while retaining executable contracts and useful documentation-link checks.
Exercise delivery snapshot edge cases directly against the guard, with representative CLI integration coverage for local, direct verify, and CI entry points and failure propagation.
Record concrete before/after test or process measurements, limitations, and verification evidence. No new dependencies or orchestration framework.

title: Clarify minimum code review coverage and finding severity
acceptance_criteria: Review covers correctness, simplicity, security, and performance where relevant, retaining existing edge-case, scope, test, and architecture checks.
Findings require concrete evidence, impact, severity, and a clear distinction between required fixes and optional suggestions. Unresolved required fixes block approval; style preferences do not.
Keep the change within the reviewer prompt and normal work-item/evidence files. No new tools, dependencies, test cases, or review stages.

title: Require unambiguous final review approval and evidence
acceptance_criteria: State and binding consume one final-review loading/parsing path, retaining exact pinned historical report selection and supported historical formats.
Approval requires one unambiguous approved verdict; conflicting or duplicate verdict declarations fail and quoted/fenced examples cannot supply approval.
Required review evidence sections contain content; empty or comment-only bodies and headings alone cannot satisfy evidence.
Digest interpretation stays shared and unambiguous, while whole-index binding, reviewed maintenance, existing command diagnostics, and historical report bytes remain protected.
Focused regressions exercise both existing validator interfaces, valid reports, and historical compatibility; no framework, dependency, or unrelated architecture changes.

title: Share project-gate composition validation with adoption audit
acceptance_criteria: Audit and verification contracts share validation of the supported ordered verify command, retaining the bootstrap form without a project stage and requiring the project stage for adoption.

Adoption rejects missing or empty project commands, textual mentions or aliases instead of the exact project invocation, missing/reordered/duplicate stages, and shell forms outside the supported fail-fast composition with clear findings.
Existing execution tests still prove stage order and failure propagation. Focused audit regressions cover false positives and valid composition without multiplying subprocess pipelines.
Documentation explains the supported composition and limits: structural validation does not prove project command coverage or correctness. No shell-parser framework or dependency is added.

title: Align inventory decision validation with its schema
acceptance_criteria: Each typecheck, test, and build decision contains exactly one command or notApplicable property with a non-whitespace string value.
Reject both properties even when the second value is blank or has the wrong type. Retain TARGET_DECISION_INVALID and existing deployable-build checks.
Preserve valid decision strings exactly. Direct fixtures cover invalid shapes and valid alternatives across all three decision slots.
Keep the fix within inventory validation and focused regression coverage. No new dependency or schema interpreter.

title: Share feature-queue validation between state and binding
acceptance_criteria: State and binding share queue reading, feature validation, normalized identity, allowed status, and single-active-feature policy.
Binding rejects malformed, duplicate, unsafe-ID, invalid-status, and multiple-active queues before selecting approval. Valid whitespace-padded IDs use the same report identity as state.
Preserve existing state diagnostics, binding queue/reference diagnostic aliases, exact legacy exemptions, approval selection, evidence traversal, and digest/maintenance behavior.
Focused interface tests cover invalid queue parity and valid normalized IDs. Remove the permissive binding reader; add no dependency or general workflow engine.

title: Separate bootstrap history pins from reusable validation
acceptance_criteria: Move the existing three definition hashes and four paired review hashes unchanged into one optional repository data file. Reusable validators default to no historical exceptions when the file is absent.
Reject malformed or unreadable supplied history with a clear finding. Preserve exact definition/report hash verification, canonical fallback, and normal state/binding evidence requirements.
Fresh adoption copies unchanged validator source, omits the history file, and no longer rewrites TypeScript maps. Keep historical-only tests separable from reusable contracts.
Focused tests prove preserved history, modified/reused-ID rejection, absent/malformed history behavior, and fresh adoption. Update adoption guidance; add no dependency or plugin system.

title: Define tool-agnostic model tiers per task and role
acceptance_criteria: harness.models.json defines cost tiers, task tiers, risky-review triggers, and the default task tier for each role. It names no vendor, tool, or model.
Each role file states its task tier, and the stated tier matches the config.
docs/model-routing.md explains when to use each tier and when review escalates to the risky-review tier.
docs/model-adapters.md shows how to map cost tiers to a specific tool. It is optional and is not required by the gate.
A harness test validates the config shape, role consistency, and the absence of vendor names in the config.
